findings.title: A double-click on a row's name now toggles it once instead of not at all
findings.body: Before this change, a double-click on a row's text ran the row's `onClick` twice, and each click called `setFixing([finding.path], !fixing)` (line 217), so the two toggles cancelled out. With the new guard, the first click's mousedown collapses the selection, so the first click toggles. The second mousedown selects the word, and the second click then sees `window.getSelection()` non-empty and returns at line 216. Net effect: a double-click now flips the row once, which the PR does not mention. The guard was meant for a drag that selects a name. If the one-toggle result is not wanted, a double-click on the text could be handled as a no-op, or the guard could be limited to a selection that started in this press. The author should decide which result they want and say so in the PR.

findings.title: Any existing text selection in the window suppresses a row toggle
findings.body: The guard reads the document-wide selection, not one created by the current press. If a mousedown on the row does not collapse an earlier selection, a selection made elsewhere (the intro paragraph, the group description, or another row's name) makes the next click on this row do nothing. The row does not change and no message says why, so the user has to click again. I could not confirm from the repository whether Chromium/Electron collapses the selection on mousedown for a press on a row's padding or text; `reconcile.module.css:277-279` sets no `user-select` rule. If the selection is always collapsed on mousedown, this is not a problem. Question for the author: has a click on the row been checked after selecting text in another part of the dialog?

findings.title: Selection case sits in a test whose name does not cover it, and the spy is restored only on success
findings.body: The new block (lines 368-374) is added to the test named "a click anywhere on a selectable row toggles it, not only on the 16 px box". Nothing in that name says a click with selected text must not toggle, so a reader looking for coverage of the copy case will not find it. Give the selection case its own `it(...)`. Also, `selection.mockRestore()` at line 374 runs only if the assertion before it passes. If `expect(box).toBeChecked()` at line 373 fails, the `getSelection` mock stays in place for the rest of the file, and `afterEach` (line 65) does not restore it. Use `try/finally` or `afterEach(() => vi.restoreAllMocks())`. The mock also returns a fake selection object, so the test checks only the early return. It does not check that a real drag-select produces a click on the `li`.

contracts.action: Click on a selectable finding row whose document selection has text: the click is ignored and the row does not toggle
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/library/reconcile/reconcile-dialog.tsx:217 (the same setFixing([finding.path], !fixing) toggle, now skipped when the guard returns); the checkbox's own toggle at reconcile-dialog.tsx:230 is unchanged and does not check the selection
contracts.before_after: Before: every click on the row that is not on an input calls setFixing([finding.path], !fixing) (line 217). After: the handler returns at line 216 when window.getSelection() has text, so setFixing (reconcile-store.ts:112-120) is not called.
contracts.visible_effect: After selecting a name by dragging over it and clicking the row, the row keeps its ticked or unticked state. A double-click on the name now flips the row once, where before the two clicks cancelled out.
contracts.failure_mode: If mousedown does not collapse an earlier selection, a selection made elsewhere in the dialog makes the next click on the row do nothing, with no feedback. Nothing is lost: the user can click again.
contracts.open_question: Does a mousedown on a row's padding or text collapse an existing document selection in Chromium/Electron? If it does, the stale-selection failure cannot happen. The repository cannot settle this; it needs a manual check in the packaged app.

contracts.action: New call to window.getSelection()?.toString() on every row click that is not on an input
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/library/reconcile/reconcile-dialog.tsx:214 (the existing closest("input") early return, which has the same shape)
contracts.before_after: Before: no selection read. After: one read per row click. If getSelection() returns null, the optional chain yields undefined, the guard is falsy, and the toggle runs as before.
contracts.visible_effect: None beyond the guard in the row above.
contracts.failure_mode: If getSelection() is null, the toggle proceeds (same as before). No error is thrown and nothing is shown.

thread_replies.reply: Confirmed in 59f6d481. The row's click handler returns when `window.getSelection()` has text (reconcile-dialog.tsx:216), and the test at reconcile.test.tsx:368-374 covers that case. Keeping text selectable is fine.
